clue.text: Independent's gone for antagonist of Shakespeare

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for Independent
'long gone' and 'long ago' mean the same: past

explanation.surface: The newspaper's staff has walked out, as if in search of a Shakespearean villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so the wordplay reads 'I is AGO'; the italics on Independent are only the paper's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is Othello's scheming enemy, the great antagonist in Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: After disturbance, go and arrest Stranglers in Chicago

indicators.note: the words go and arrest are disturbed, knocked out of their order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter; 'and' just joins the two words

explanation.surface: A gangland scene: after a riot, the Chicago police go and arrest the killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranglers' looks like the name of a British punk band, but here it means things that strangle; 'in Chicago' flags the American spelling with one T.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrotes are cords or wires used for strangling; GARROTE is the usual American spelling of British garrotte.

clue.text: Tart detailed swinging first of ill-advised punches

indicators.note: de-tailed: the last letter, the tail, is cut from the word
only the opening letter of ill-advised is wanted
the I punches its way into the middle of ACD

blocks.note: AC/DC is slang for bisexual, swinging both ways; with its tail C cut off it is ACD
first letter of ill-advised

explanation.surface: A tart detailed swinging a few ill-judged punches, as in a bar-room brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' pretends to be a person in the surface; it is the adjective meaning sour. AC/DC is informal for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart taste is sharp and sour, which is what acid means as an adjective.

clue.text: Diminutive but refined French leader of maverick party to set about government

indicators.note: only the leading letter of maverick is taken to start the answer
IN ON is placed around, set about, the G

blocks.note: leader, first letter, of maverick
to be party to a secret is to be in on it
G is a standard abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A small but polished French leader of a rebel party is poised to take on the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French leader' tempts you to look for a president; 'French' belongs to the definition, marking MIGNON as a French word, and 'leader of maverick' is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mignon is French for small and dainty, used in English for something delicately pretty, as in filet mignon.

clue.text: Now I have it accepted (money from hock)

indicators.note: money, M, is taken from the word for hock

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange
hock is a joint of ham, the lower part of the leg
M is short for money, as in M1 or M3 money supply

explanation.surface: Someone gets their pawned goods accepted at last and cries out that they have the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hock' looks like pawning or German wine, but it is a cut of ham; the brackets hold the wordplay for the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Aha is what you exclaim at the moment of understanding: now I have it.

clue.text: Statesman's a crusty sort, adopting son, perhaps - but not daughter

indicators.note: the churl takes the child into his home, so CHIL goes inside CHURL
D, daughter, is left out of CHILD

blocks.note: a churl is a surly, bad-tempered person
a son is one example of a child, so 'perhaps'
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A gruff statesman takes in a son, but not a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman's' reads as 'Statesman is'; 'son, perhaps' is a definition by example, since a son is one kind of child.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's wartime prime minister, the archetypal statesman.

clue.text: Fresh victuals are picked out from rare refined plants

indicators.note: the letters ARE are removed from rare, leaving R
the victuals are made fresh, reworked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
RARE with ARE picked out of it

explanation.surface: Fresh food chosen from rare, carefully bred plants, like a gourmet's kitchen garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is part of the machinery, not a verb: those three letters are removed from 'rare', leaving R to join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A cultivar is a plant variety produced by selective breeding, refined from its wild form.

clue.text: Sunday: flat set for renovation - but not with any tenacity

indicators.note: the letters are set aside to be renovated, rebuilt in a new form

blocks.note: all thirteen letters, taken as printed

explanation.surface: On Sunday the flat is set to be done up, but the workers show little staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is the three words run together; the colon is only surface punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To act unsteadfastly is to act without firmness or perseverance, not with any tenacity.

clue.text: Old boy besotted with reading and writing? New Romantic!

indicators.note: besotted means drunk, so the letters of old boy stagger out of order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
two of the three Rs: reading, writing and arithmetic
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A former pupil infatuated with literacy turns out to be a New Romantic, the 1980s pop movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Romantic' looks like one phrase for an 80s pop fan; split it, and New is N while Romantic alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was one of the great English Romantic poets.

clue.text: Brooks's direction waiving unneeded extras

blocks.note: N, north, is a compass direction
the possessive turned round: Brooks's direction is the direction of brooks
rills are small brooks

explanation.surface: It reads like the way a film by Mel Brooks was directed: plain, with nothing wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Brooks look like the director Mel Brooks; it is just streams, and 'Brooks's direction' is rearranged as 'direction of brooks'.
explanation.definitionFit: No-frills means basic, stripped of any unnecessary extras.

clue.text: ...this report in religious office

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for religious office is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a deanery is the office or residence of a dean

explanation.surface: The tail end of a church story: this report was filed from inside a cathedral office.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join the clue to its own number: '10 ... this' means the number system in which 10 is written, so 'this' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Denary means based on ten, the decimal system, which is how the clue number 10 is written.

clue.text: "It's rather rude, the way the swastika letter ends. Yours, H. Himmler & co."

definitions.note: a clause describing the quality, standing for the noun

indicators.note: only the end letters of the three words are kept

blocks.note: last letters of the, swastika and letter
thine is the old form of yours
Heinrich Himmler headed the SS, the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A shocked reader objects to a letter bearing a swastika and signed off by Himmler and his men.
explanation.walkthrough: The sign-off 'Yours, H. Himmler & co.' looks like part of the letter; each piece is wordplay, with 'Yours' as THINE and Himmler's organisation as SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthiness is crude, bawdy frankness: something that is rather rude.

clue.text: Transmuter compiler's set up in aluminium box

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up turns it bottom to top
'in' places the setter's reversed I'M in the box, inside CHEST rather than beside it

blocks.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
compiler's = compiler is = I'M, the setter speaking of themself
a chest is a large box

explanation.surface: A setter describes their own word-changing trade, packed into a metal box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compiler' is a crossword setter's word for themself, so compiler's is I'M; 'set up' suits a down clue, where reversing reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist tries to transmute base metals into gold.

clue.text: Two people after this trip not delighted to win the prize?

definitions.text: Two people after this trip not delighted to win the prize?

blocks.note: the straight reading: a couple takes to the floor, trip being old slang for dance

blocks.clueFragment: not delighted to win the prize?
blocks.note: the pun: the winners are not de-lighted but caught in the spotlight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Delighted' breaks as de-lighted, lights off; the winners of a spot dance are the couple caught in the spotlight when the music stops, so they are anything but de-lighted.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot dance is a ballroom dance in which a prize goes to the couple spotlighted when the music stops.

clue.text: Back home from what accommodates those cautioned VIPs

indicators.note: home, IN, is taken from the sin bin
what is left is read back to front

blocks.note: at home means in
in rugby and ice hockey, a cautioned player is sent to the sin bin

explanation.surface: The important people cautioned by police are sent back home.
explanation.walkthrough: The sin bin is the penalty area where a sports player sent off for a spell waits; remove IN and reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibs, as in 'his nibs', is a mocking term for a self-important person, so VIPs.

clue.text: Potential for sauce you shouldn't have noticed in rude P-words ordered by century

indicators.note: the rude P-words are put in a new order
the century stands by, next to, the rearranged words
TA is spotted inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
fodder taken letter for letter
what you say when given a present, meaning thanks; ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: Cheeky talk you shouldn't have noticed, among rude words starting with P, sorted by the hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' hints at cheek, but it is the custard you pour; 'you shouldn't have' is the polite protest on getting a gift, so TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard powder is a packet mix that becomes custard, a sweet sauce, once milk is added: it has the potential to be sauce.

clue.text: Time with nice car occupying the 8am-4pm period comedy?

indicators.note: the car occupies the slot where the middle letter was, taking its place

blocks.note: a day is a period of time
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce
8am to 4pm is the middle eight of the day's 24 hours, so the middle letter of DAY

explanation.surface: Someone on the day shift turns up in a posh car: a bit of a comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8am-4pm span is the middle third of a day, so the ROLLER replaces DAY's middle letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is dry humour or comic behaviour, so comedy.

clue.text: Approach that helps 8 with 11?

indicators.note: 8 is placed with 11, the two answers written side by side

blocks.note: 8 Down is LORD BYRON, which ends in N
11 Across is EARTHINESS, which opens with EAR

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solving tip: which approach helps you crack clue 8 and clue 11 together?
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers stand for the answers to 8 Down and 11 Across; written one after the other, lord byroN EARthiness, the answer bridges the join, which is how it helps them.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to near is to come closer, a plain synonym of approach.

clue.text: This country's cultivating upper-class airs and graces at last

indicators.note: only the final letter of graces is wanted
cultivating works the letters over like soil into a new shape

blocks.note: U is the standard label for upper-class
fodder taken letter for letter
the last letter of graces

explanation.surface: A nation is accused of cultivating aristocratic airs and graces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This country's' reads as 'this country is', with the fodder following.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Russia is one country among many, and 'This' points at the answer as the country meant.

clue.text: Cryptic St. Station

indicators.note: it tells you to read St. literally as its parts rather than as saint or street

blocks.note: the two letters as printed
the letters are followed by the full stop, so ST and a point
the full stop is a point

explanation.walkthrough: 'St.' wants to be saint or street; spelt out, it is the letters ST and a point, the full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is a position from which things are viewed, a station.

clue.text: Stratford thesps on road taking a little breather

indicators.note: in an across clue the thesps come on, after, the road
the RSC takes the A inside

blocks.note: the A1, Britain's Great North Road, written as AI
the Royal Shakespeare Company, based at Stratford-upon-Avon
taken as printed

explanation.surface: Actors from Stratford on tour stop for a short breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a little breather' reads as a rest; 'taking a' is the wordplay and 'little breather' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An air sac is a small air-filled cavity in the lungs of birds or insects, a little breathing organ.

clue.text: Choice of casing for chromium storage structure

indicators.note: the outside letters of chromium form a case around the choice

blocks.note: the outer letters of chromium
'or' is the word that offers a choice

explanation.surface: A choice of chrome casing for a storage unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chromium' tempts you to use its symbol Cr; here only its outer letters C and M are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A corm is a swollen underground stem base that stores food for a plant, like a crocus.

clue.text: For such protection, make Eve a cardinal

definitions.text: For such protection, make Eve a cardinal

blocks.note: the straight reading: a coating that protects metal
the demonstration: coat EVE with Sn, tin, and it reads SEVEN, a cardinal number

explanation.walkthrough: Plate EVE with tin, chemical symbol Sn, and S-EVE-N becomes SEVEN, a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinplate is iron or steel coated with tin to protect it from rusting.

clue.text: One mooring stage

blocks.note: one who ties, as when tying up a boat
a level or rank

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is tie plus -ER: someone who ties up a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one who ties, as when mooring; a tier is also a level or stage.

clue.text: Non-standard system of lines: what's ETA of Spooner's train?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words, so his version of the phrase has them exchanged

blocks.note: a train runs on rail; it hands its R over and takes the T
ETA is estimated time of arrival, so a time; it takes the R, spelt RH in the verse word

explanation.surface: A timetable query about when a train will arrive on an odd branch line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'System of lines' looks like a railway network; it is verse. ETA is estimated time of arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Tail rhyme is a verse form in which rhyming couplets are followed by a shorter tail line, an unusual system of lines.

clue.text: Did someone say "bitter" bread?

indicators.note: asks what was said aloud, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: wry means bitterly ironic

explanation.surface: A diner queries whether the bread was described as bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: WRY and RYE sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Named by its grain: the dark, dense loaf baked from that cereal's flour is ordered simply by the grain's name.
